examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, у вас тут зеркало сломанное.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, you have a broken mirror here.
He smashes the mirror on her car.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, у вас тут зеркало сломанное.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, you have a broken mirror here.

examples.text: Это слово «сломанный» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'broken' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломанный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('broken').
emphatic at the start of a sentence

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('even, quits').

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: He smashes the mirror on her car.

examples.text: Это слово «разбивать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to smash' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'бивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to smash, break'.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: А она типа не при делах.
examples.trans: And she acts like she had nothing to do with it.

examples.text: Да я не про это. Кто этот тип в коридоре?
examples.trans: That's not what I mean. Who was that guy in the corridor?

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'like, sort of' in everyday speech.

при.gloss: in the presence of, in front of; at, under

meanings.en: in the presence of, in front of (a person)

examples.text: Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Why did you just say that in front of him?

examples.text: Не говори об этом при детях.
examples.trans: Don't talk about this in front of the children.

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный.
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident.
He answered in a calm, confident voice.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный. Что конкретно?
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident. What specifically?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: the thing that ends is the subject
деньги закончились = the money ran out

examples.text: Всё, выборы закончились. Тебя начальник ждёт.
examples.trans: That's it, the election is over. Your boss is waiting for you.
